published_statement: (i) ECs, as restated (Curiel 1405.0403; MM&V 1702.05915): WEC T_ab xi^a xi^b >= 0 for every timelike xi; NEC T_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for every null k; SEC (T_ab - T g_ab/2) xi^a xi^b >= 0; DEC = WEC + causal flux. Type-I forms: NEC rho+p_i >= 0; WEC adds rho >= 0; SEC adds rho+Sum p >= 0; DEC |p_i| <= rho. (ii) Chronology (KRW gr-qc/9603012v2 p.2-3, verbatim): 'any spacetime obtained by starting with a globally hyperbolic spacetime and then smoothly deforming the metric in a compact region so that the spacetime admits closed timelike curves must possess a compactly generated Cauchy horizon'; 'the weak energy condition must be violated in any spacetime with a compactly generated Cauchy horizon with noncompact partial Cauchy surface S [23 = Hawking 1992]'; 'Under some additional assumptions, violation of the averaged null energy condition also must occur'. Visser gr-qc/0204022v2 p.14: chronology protection is a CONJECTURE ('Despite a decade's work we do not know for certain'). (iii) PMT (EHLS 1110.2087v2 p.2): 'In the time-symmetric case, we have that P = 0 and the dominant energy condition becomes the assumption that the scalar curvature of g is nonnegative'; rigidity (Huang-Lee 1706.03732v3 p.2): 'if E = 0, then (M, g) is isometric to Euclidean space.'
published_hypotheses: EC: definitions quantifying over ALL timelike/null vectors at a point; 'holds' needs every observer, 'fails' needs one; effective (rho,p_i) forms need Hawking-Ellis type I; physical = geometric form only with the Einstein equation

Hawking 1992 (via KRW): time-orientable spacetime with a closed achronal edgeless S, D+(S) != I+(S), and all past-directed null generators of H+(S) entering and remaining in a compact K (compactly generated Cauchy horizon); S NONCOMPACT for the WEC conclusion; 'additional assumptions' (unnamed in KRW) for the ANEC conclusion; Einstein equation (implicit)
Chronology protection itself: a conjecture, not a theorem (Visser 0204022 p.1, p.14; KRW p.1 'giving support to')
Tipler 1977 Thm 5 (via Borde): closed-universe case, non-compact interpolating spacetime, 'mild additional assumptions' -- see sibling audit

PMT: complete asymptotically flat initial data (M,g,k), n = 3 (Schoen-Yau, Witten); DOMINANT energy condition mu >= |J|, which for k = 0 is R_g >= 0; conclusion E >= |P|; rigidity (separate argument): time-symmetric E = 0 => (M,g) Euclidean
No empirical data enter any member: each is a definition or a mathematical implication whose physical input is an energy-condition hypothesis
hypothesis_drift: ASSERTION CONTRADICTED (not a drift in the external result): phase1.py:195-197 and :537-539 say no energy condition is violated by D1-D5 with M_ADM = 0. The seated device (phase1.py:261-263 phi_device = concentric.py:163-168 potential, Phi = m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) - m/max(r,R_s), m > 0) has, exactly, 8pi(rho+p_t) = 2 e^{2Phi} lap Phi = -6 m a^2 e^{2Phi}/(r^2+a^2)^{5/2} < 0 and 8pi rho = e^{2Phi}(2 lap Phi - Phi'^2) < 0 at EVERY 0 < r < R_s: NEC, WEC, SEC and DEC all fail throughout the core (C1-C2). The tree's own phase1.py:203-204 'everything above needs M < 0' and the positive-mass shell (C2, [Phi'] = +m/R_s^2) are consistent with this.

DROPPED (named class, unnamed members): phase1.py:195-197 names 'no energy condition, no chronology theorem and no positive-mass theorem' but no member, and nothing in code checks one (canonical hypothesis 2; status_word none). The file's own standard, phase1.py:10-11 'Everything here is either proved from the definition, or measured by an instrument named at the claim. Nothing is asserted', is not met by this line -- status drift.

DROPPED (the energy-condition hypothesis of the theorems): every chronology theorem read (Hawking 1992 via KRW p.3) and the PMT (EHLS p.2) ASSUMES an energy condition (WEC; DEC / R_g >= 0). A configuration that violates the WEC cannot 'violate' them -- their hypotheses fail. So the chronology and PMT clauses of phase1.py:195-197 are true only BECAUSE the energy-condition clause of the same sentence is false for the device; the sentence presents three independent permissions where there is one violation and two consequences of it.

DROPPED (PMT rigidity): phase1.py:195-197 treats M_ADM = 0 as compatible with the PMT outright. Under the PMT's DEC, E = 0 forces a Euclidean slice (Huang-Lee p.2); the device's slice is not Euclidean (R_h(0) = -2.2163e5 < 0, C4). With the rigidity clause kept, 'no PMT violated & no EC violated & M_ADM = 0 & non-flat static' is UNSAT (z3, C6). Same sentence flagged by the sibling positive-mass-theorem audit; phase1.py:397-399 ('bare negative mass ... forbidden by the positive mass theorem') drops the DEC -- recorded there, not re-graded here.

WEAKENED-TO-VACUOUS (chronology, held configurations): a static configuration with g^{tt} = -e^{-2Phi} < 0 has t strictly increasing on every causal curve (z3, C8), hence no closed causal curve and no compactly generated Cauchy horizon: the chronology theorems' hypotheses are absent, so 'not violated' is true and vacuous. For the PASSAGE between configurations (D4(ii), formation.py F1; phase1.py:28-37) nothing in the tree checks causal structure -- OPEN, not STANDS. phase1.py:124 'it is not chronology protection' is a disclaimer, consistent with this.

DISCREPANCY (recorded, not graded here): D2 (phase1.py:23-24) requires g_s = g_0 outside a compact K, but the seated Phi outside R_s is m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) - m/r ~ -m a^2/(2 r^3) != 0 (C3; -6.25e-14 at r = 2R_s with tree values). M_ADM = 0 holds exactly (1/r coefficient 0); compact support holds only to O(r^-3). This does not move the device's EC violation (C2, pointwise in the core) nor the PMT route (needs only asymptotic flatness); it matters only for the compact-support lemma C5.

SCOPE OF THE CLASS (evidence the other way): D1-D5 as written is met by a pure-gauge member -- flat space pulled back by a compactly supported diffeomorphism moving A toward B (C7: Gaussian curvature 0 for generic f; d_s(A,B) = 10, 9.816, 9.632, 9.448). It violates no energy condition. So the literal existential reading 'D1-D5 with M_ADM = 0 does not REQUIRE a violation' is TRUE, but only through members that are flat spacetime; C6 shows every static, compactly supported, non-flat member with M_ADM = 0 violates the WEC (PMT rigidity when the slice is non-flat; C5 lemma when the slice is flat and the lapse is not).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this class. What the authors had: the energy conditions (Hawking-Ellis 1973) and the PMT (Schoen-Yau 1979/81, Witten 1981) were formulated with classical matter in view; Hawking 1992 had the Morris-Thorne-Yurtsever wormhole proposals and knew the WEC fails for quantum fields (KRW p.3 'this condition can be violated in quantum field theory'). What came later: measured Casimir forces (Lamoreaux 1997 onward), squeezed vacuum in LIGO, QEIs (Ford-Roman, Fewster), the ANEC/QNEC programme, and the 2020-2022 positive-energy warp-drive claims and their rebuttals (2105.03079). Does it change the conclusion? Evidence for 'no': each member is a definition or a mathematical implication with NO empirical input (data_at_publication), so no datum can move it; what later data did change is whether the ENERGY CONDITIONS ARE OBEYED IN NATURE (they are not, pointwise, for quantum fields -- Kontou-Sanders 2003.01815 via sibling audit), which weakens the ECs as physical laws but leaves the implications 'EC => conclusion' intact. Evidence the other way: the averaged-condition replacements (ANEC-based positivity, Penrose-Sorkin-Woolgar, contested per the sibling PMT audit) are still being settled, so which energy condition is the right hypothesis is open; that bears on how strongly the device is forbidden, not on whether it violates the pointwise ECs (it does, C2). For THIS claim the data question is moot in a sharper way: the tree's sentence is contradicted by the tree's own geometry (C2, C4, C6), with no external datum involved. Nothing here shows the external mathematics inaccurate, incomplete or wrong.
grade_evidence: The external class STANDS as published: the EC definitions, Hawking's 1992 theorem (via KRW) and the PMT with rigidity (via EHLS, Huang-Lee) are read in cached arXiv text and every re-derivation agrees. The grade is NARROWED because the tree's use of them is wider than they support, in three computed ways. (1) The energy-condition clause of phase1.py:195-197/537-539 is CONTRADICTED for the seated device: NEC, WEC, SEC and DEC fail at every 0 < r < R_s, exactly (C2). This is a contradiction of the tree's sentence, not of any external result, which is why it is not graded WRONG: no external theorem is refuted, and calling the class wrong would over-represent in the other direction. (2) The chronology and PMT clauses are true only because their energy-condition hypotheses fail (DROPPED hypotheses): with the DEC kept, 'no EC violated & M_ADM = 0 & non-flat static' is UNSAT by PMT rigidity (C6), and for held static configurations the chronology clause is vacuous (no Cauchy horizon, C8); for passages it is unchecked (OPEN). (3) Under the only reading on which the sentence is true -- 'D1-D5 with M_ADM = 0 does not require a violation' -- the witnesses are flat spacetime only (C7); every static, compactly supported, non-flat member with M_ADM = 0 violates the WEC (C5-C6). The surviving, narrowed statement is: 'a static D1-D5 configuration with M_ADM = 0 is not forbidden by the chronology or positive-mass theorems, because it violates the energy conditions those theorems assume; the seated device violates NEC, WEC, SEC and DEC throughout its core.' Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters. Not OPEN overall: the class is read (via restatement) and the tree's claim is checked; only the passage (dynamic) chronology question is OPEN and named.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restating phase1.py:195-197 as the narrowed statement above (an energy-condition violation acknowledged, the chronology and PMT clauses stated as consequences), with an instrument named at the claim. To WRONG: only a refutation of an external member -- e.g. a counterexample to PMT rigidity for complete AF time-symmetric data with R_g >= 0, or to Hawking's WEC theorem -- none is known or shown here. To OPEN on the chronology clause as a whole: showing the passage family g_s (formation.py) can develop a compactly generated Cauchy horizon; a check that it cannot would close the passage part. Reading Hawking 1992, Tipler 1977 and Schoen-Yau/Witten at source (NAMED-NOT-READ now) could add hypotheses but, on the restatements, not remove the energy-condition hypothesis the narrowing rests on.
